claims.text: You must sign in to Gleaniverse to access the Glean Support Center.
Logins from the legacy support portal were not migrated, so users need a Gleaniverse account.
Before opening a ticket, search Glean Docs, ask Query, and check the Glean status page for known issues.
The Support Center has two entry points: Ask Query in the top navigation and the support widget in the bottom-right corner.
Conversations are available to all users and are the best starting point for most requests.
Tickets formally track issues that need follow-up or escalation. They are best for bug reports, outages, and requests that need a documented resolution.
If a conversation needs escalation, support can convert it into a ticket.
Ticket creation is available to Designated Support Contacts as defined in the Glean Support Agreement. Contact the Glean account team to be set up as one.
To create a ticket, a Designated Support Contact opens the support widget, selects Create a ticket, describes the issue, selects a priority, and submits.
To start a conversation, open the support widget and select Send us a message. The assistant triages the request and guides you to a ticket if it cannot resolve the issue.
Users who are not Designated Support Contacts can start a conversation or ask their Glean administrator to submit a ticket.
Non-entitled users can be cc'd on a conversation or ticket with a Designated Support Contact, for example to supply screenshots or reproduction steps.
Email to help@glean.com is triaged by the AI assistant first and handed to a human agent for Designated Support Contacts.
Submit feature requests and product feedback on the Feedback and Ideas board in Gleaniverse.
A complete ticket includes an issue description with reproduction steps, exact error messages, date and time with timezone, user impact, the relevant document URL, and screenshots or recordings.
The customer must assess business impact and urgency when selecting a priority.

Priority levels are Low, Normal, High, and Urgent. Low covers non-critical issues such as general product inquiries and feature requests. Over-escalating priority can slow resolution for genuinely critical issues.

Urgent examples: the Service is unavailable to all users, or a security incident is detected. High examples: the Service is unavailable to a subset of users, or a new release materially harmed existing connected applications. Normal example: results are incomplete or truncated from known connected sources.
Only incidents submitted through the Glean support portal are eligible for SLA response times. Response times cannot be tracked accurately outside the portal.

Standard Support initial response times: Urgent 1 business day, High 2 business days, Normal and Low 1 business week. Premium: Urgent 1 hour, High 4 business hours, Normal 1 business day, Low 2 business days.
Standard Support provides 24x5 hours and 1 to 4 Designated Support Contacts. Premium provides 24x7 for Urgent incidents only and 1 to 10 Designated Support Contacts. The Order Form sets the tier.
Designated Support Contacts view company-wide conversations and tickets through the Go to customer portal banner in the support widget. Do not go directly to ticket.glean.com.
The Tickets section in the support widget appears only after the first ticket is created.
Designated Support Contacts should know the deployment and configuration, have admin access to connected applications, prioritize accurately, and use self-service resources first.
Glean Support runs a monthly live troubleshooting session on the second Thursday of each month, working through questions in small groups.
For bugs and errors in a Glean instance, file a support ticket. For questions, best practices, or feature requests, use the community.
Keep sensitive information out: do not share confidential or personal data.
